nodes.line: You are not from around the corner, are you.

It has been three weeks. I am sending back 54 papers a day from Erskineville and paying to have them collected, which is a business model somebody invented on purpose. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. I'll put the kettle on for when you're back.

Nobody else has offered, so. They will drop my Erskineville order if I can show $43 of turnover on the other side of the shop by the week of the show. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. Just do not come back empty-handed.
Take a breath. Then say the whole thing.

choices.text: The Better Rate, Erskineville — that's done.

nodes.line: No dramas. Come back when you are bored.
Half of this suburb has walked past already. Not one stopped.

The council knows and the council does not care. I do the Erskineville round from half six and for the last fortnight somebody has been taking the papers off the front steps behind me. It is not the money. It has stopped being the money. I will know if you skipped a bit.

I have been putting it off since Easter. There is a dog on the Erskineville round that has had two of my bags and a laminated notice that was not even mine. I did try the official route, for what that was worth. Say nothing to anyone on the way.
Go on then. What did you find.

choices.text: The Dog on Ash Street, Erskineville — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.
Whatever it is, I have had worse this week.

Before you say anything: yes, I know. Nine of us at Erskineville have gone in on the same numbers since the week of the show and one of us has stopped putting money in. I have got a photo on my phone but it is useless. Do not make a scene about it.

It is not a police matter and I have checked. The agency at St Peters closed six months before Erskineville started struggling, and I would very much like to know what they know. I am aware how that sounds. Ask for me by name at the counter.
You came back. That already puts you ahead.

choices.text: The Other Agency, Erskineville — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.

npcs.name: Emre, panel beater at Bank Street

nodes.line: Sit down if you like. Nobody else is using it.

It has been three weeks. There has been a car in the Bank Street yard since every second Friday with a bucket of odd keys on the passenger seat and no owner answering. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. I'll put the kettle on for when you're back.

Nobody else has offered, so. Now that it is documented, Bank Street is owed $38 in storage and the only person who can pay it is the person not answering. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. Just do not come back empty-handed.
Right. Tell me and do not soften it.

choices.text: The Unclaimed Falcon, Bank Street — that's done.
Storage Fees, Bank Street — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.
You will have to speak up, the trains are in.

The council knows and the council does not care. I am in my first year at Bank Street and I have to log 75 hours on a job I am not allowed to touch on my own. It is not the money. It has stopped being the money. I will know if you skipped a bit.

I have been putting it off since Easter. Somebody has been coming into the Bank Street yard after the middle of the news to use the air line, and last week they used the compressor as well. I did try the official route, for what that was worth. Say nothing to anyone on the way.
I have been thinking about it all day. Out with it.

choices.text: First Year, Bank Street — that's done.
The Air Line, Bank Street — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.

npcs.name: Seanan, the bloke whose car it is at Bank Street

nodes.line: I have got about four minutes before I am needed.

Before you say anything: yes, I know. My car has been at Bank Street since every second Friday and every time I ring, the quote has grown by about $75. I have got a photo on my phone but it is useless. Do not make a scene about it.

It is not a police matter and I have checked. The insurance assessor who signs off every job at Bank Street works out of QVB, and he has never once seen the car he is assessing. I am aware how that sounds. Ask for me by name at the counter.
Well? I can read your face from here.

choices.text: My Own Car, Bank Street — that's done.
The Assessor, Bank Street — that's done.

nodes.line: Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.

npcs.name: Arun, shop manager at Point Clare

nodes.line: Ah. Someone with two working legs.

It has been three weeks. People leave things at the Point Clare roller door after five in the morning and by morning it is rained on and it is our problem and our tip fee. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. I'll put the kettle on for when you're back.

Nobody else has offered, so. The photos worked, which means Point Clare can claim back the $55 we have paid to throw away other people's furniture since every second Friday. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. Just do not come back empty-handed.
Sit. Talk. Then I will decide how I feel.

choices.text: Dumped Out the Back, Point Clare — that's done.
The Tip Fee, Point Clare — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.
You are early. Or late. I have lost track.

The council knows and the council does not care. Something came into Point Clare on every second Friday in a box of paperbacks that I do not think the family meant to give away. It is not the money. It has stopped being the money. I will know if you skipped a bit.

I have been putting it off since Easter. Two people have been coming into the Point Clare sorting room since every second Friday and taking the good stock before it reaches the floor, and one of them volunteers here. I did try the official route, for what that was worth. Say nothing to anyone on the way.
You have got that look. Good or bad, out with it.

choices.text: The Good Box, Point Clare — that's done.
Sorting Room, Point Clare — that's done.

nodes.line: Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.

npcs.name: Milena, volunteer driver at Point Clare

nodes.line: Been here since before it was like this. Go on.

Before you say anything: yes, I know. I do the Point Clare pick-ups in a van with 95 thousand on it and a door that only opens if you know about it. I have got a photo on my phone but it is useless. Do not make a scene about it.

It is not a police matter and I have checked. Everything Point Clare cannot sell goes to a warehouse at Tascott, and nobody there has ever answered a phone in my hearing. I am aware how that sounds. Ask for me by name at the counter.
Before you start: did anyone see you.

choices.text: The Van, Point Clare — that's done.
Head Office, Point Clare — that's done.
